lesson.child_mission: Musical instruments make sound when a part vibrates: strings, skins, air columns or solid bars.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Match instrument→vibrating part: violin; bongo; xylophone bar.

FEEDBACK
String; skin; solid bar (accept air for wind if named wind instrument instead).

WATCH FOR
Saying “the music comes from electricity” for an acoustic guitar ignores the vibrating string.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Classify eight instruments by what vibrates. Build one simple instrument from scrap and label the vibrating part.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Musical instruments make sound when a part vibrates: strings, skins, air columns or solid bars.
materials: Optional: safe everyday objects for observation
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Classify eight instruments by what vibrates. Build one simple instrument from scrap and label the vibrating part. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: String; skin; solid bar (accept air for wind if named wind instrument instead). Reasoning: I used instrument by attending to vibrate rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Saying “the music comes from electricity” for an acoustic guitar ignores the vibrating string. Correction: String; skin; solid bar (accept air for wind if named wind instrument instead). Why: the correction restores accurate use of instrument.

Parent: Likely misconception: Saying “the music comes from electricity” for an acoustic guitar ignores the vibrating string. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses instrument. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about instrument, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Require a new example, named observations and a claim–evidence link. / Require misconception + corrected claim + evidence reason..
